evidence.description: The initializer launches an asynchronous Task to retrieve credentials without providing a mechanism to handle the result or potential errors before the object is fully initialized.

candidates.explanation: Launching an unawaited Task in an initializer can lead to race conditions where the object's properties (like isLoggedIn or tokens) are in an inconsistent state for the caller immediately after initialization.
candidates.title: Unawaited Task in Initializer

evidence.description: The setupTokensWithCredentials method updates multiple properties (idToken, accessToken, refreshToken, isLoggedIn) and then launches a new Task to dispatch state changes.

candidates.explanation: Updating multiple state properties and then launching a detached Task to notify other systems can cause 'tearing' or inconsistent states where the internal properties have changed but the external state management system has not yet been notified.
candidates.title: Inconsistent State Propagation

evidence.description: The retrieveSSOCredentials method uses a conditional cast to NativeToWebSSOAuth0Provider to access specific functionality.

candidates.explanation: Using type casting to check for specific capabilities of a protocol implementation is a code smell that suggests the protocol (Auth0ProviderProtocol) is not sufficiently expressive of the required behaviors.
candidates.title: Type Casting for Protocol Capabilities
